alt.en: A tall clear drinking glass on a grey ground, its flared bowl engraved with a large open rose, buds and leaves on a thorny stem, and white spiral threads twisting down inside the stem.
alt.es: Una copa alta de vidrio transparente sobre fondo gris, con el cáliz acampanado grabado con una gran rosa abierta, capullos y hojas en un tallo con espinas, y hilos blancos en espiral que bajan por dentro del pie.

caption.en: A wineglass of about 1745 engraved with a rose and buds, catalogued by the Metropolitan Museum of Art as a wineglass with Jacobite emblems: the cause Carolina's father and grandfather fought for in the rising.
caption.es: Una copa de vino de hacia 1745 grabada con una rosa y capullos, que el Metropolitan Museum of Art cataloga como copa con emblemas jacobitas: la causa por la que lucharon el padre y el abuelo de Carolina en el levantamiento.

source: Wineglass with Jacobite emblems, ca. 1745, glass, height 18.1 cm; photograph DP349852
library: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (Edward Holbrook Collection, Gift of Mrs. Edward Holbrook and John S. Holbrook, 1921)
licenceEvidence: Met Collection API record https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/194725: "isPublicDomain": true; Met Open Access images of public-domain works are released under Creative Commons Zero (https://metmuseum.github.io/: "The Metropolitan Museum of Art has waived all copyright"). The photograph is the Met's own. Object made about 1745, maker unknown.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Edward Holbrook Collection, Gift of Mrs. Edward Holbrook and John S. Holbrook, 1921

alt.en: A cropped book page of plain type, one paragraph beginning "In 1766 was born the chief ornament of the Gask line" and quoting "Carolina, after the King, at Gask, Aug. 16th, 1766."
alt.es: Recorte de una página de libro en letra sencilla, un párrafo que empieza "In 1766 was born the chief ornament of the Gask line" y cita "Carolina, after the King, at Gask, Aug. 16th, 1766."

caption.en: Carolina's birth as Kington Oliphant printed it from the family papers in The Jacobite Lairds of Gask (London, 1870), quoting her father's list of births: "Carolina, after the King, at Gask, Aug. 16th, 1766."
caption.es: El nacimiento de Carolina tal como lo publicó Kington Oliphant a partir de los papeles de la familia en The Jacobite Lairds of Gask (Londres, 1870), citando la lista de nacimientos de su padre: "Carolina, after the King, at Gask, Aug. 16th, 1766" ("Carolina, por el rey, en Gask, 16 de agosto de 1766").

source: T. L. Kington Oliphant, The Jacobite Lairds of Gask (London: Charles Griffin and Co., for the Grampian Club, 1870), p. 349; cropped to the paragraph beginning "In 1766 was born"
library: Allen County Public Library Genealogy Center (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1870; T. L. Kington Oliphant died 1902; the page quotes Laurence Oliphant (died 1792) and Bishop Robert Forbes (died 1775). Internet Archive record: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Allen County Public Library Genealogy Center, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: The top of a printed page headed "Advertisement to Volume Sixth" and numbered 3, seven lines of text in which the editors thank "the author of the much-admired song, 'The Land of the Leal'" and say "they fear to wound a delicacy which shrinks from all observation".
alt.es: La parte superior de una página impresa con el encabezado "Advertisement to Volume Sixth" y el número 3, siete líneas en las que los editores dan las gracias a "the author of the much-admired song, 'The Land of the Leal'" y dicen "they fear to wound a delicacy which shrinks from all observation".

caption.en: The Scotish Minstrel's last volume (Edinburgh, January 1824) thanks the author of "The Land of the Leal" for many of its verses without naming her, for fear of wounding "a delicacy which shrinks from all observation".
caption.es: El último volumen de The Scotish Minstrel (Edimburgo, enero de 1824) agradece a quien escribió "The Land of the Leal" muchos de sus versos sin nombrarla, por miedo a herir "una delicadeza que rehúye toda mirada".

source: R. A. Smith, arranger, The Scotish Minstrel: A Selection from the Vocal Melodies of Scotland, Ancient & Modern, vols. 5 and 6 (Edinburgh: Robert Purdie; catalogued 1821), vol. 6, "Advertisement to Volume Sixth", p. 3 (dated on p. 4 "Edinburgh, January 1824"); cropped to the top paragraph, above the footnote
library: University of Western Ontario (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed Edinburgh 1824, the editors unnamed; R. A. Smith died 1829, Robert Purdie the publisher in the 1830s; the page names James Hogg, the Ettrick Shepherd (died 1835). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of Western Ontario, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music numbered 107 and headed "Will Ye No Come Back Again?", marked "In moderate time." and "Finlay Dun.", with a voice line over a piano part, three verses under the notes beginning "Bon-nie Charlie's now a-wa", a chorus "Will ye no come back again?", and verses 4 and 5 printed in two columns at the foot.
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el número 107 y el título "Will Ye No Come Back Again?", marcada "In moderate time." y "Finlay Dun.", con la línea de canto sobre la parte de piano, tres estrofas bajo las notas que empiezan "Bon-nie Charlie's now a-wa", el estribillo "Will ye no come back again?" y las estrofas 4 y 5 en dos columnas al pie.

caption.en: The page our arrangement is read from, in Oliver Ditson's Gems of Scottish Song (Boston, the printing catalogued as 1883), headed only "Finlay Dun.", with the chorus's high second line marked "a piacere".
caption.es: La página de la que está tomado nuestro arreglo, en Gems of Scottish Song de Oliver Ditson (Boston, la impresión catalogada como de 1883), con el encabezado "Finlay Dun." y nada más, y la aguda segunda línea del estribillo marcada "a piacere".

source: Gems of Scottish Song: A Collection of the Most Beautiful Scotch Ballads, Set to Music (Boston: Oliver Ditson & Company; the printing catalogued as 1883; editor not named), p. 107, "Will Ye No Come Back Again?", "Finlay Dun."
library: Internet Archive (book scanned by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed Boston, catalogued 1883 (US, before 1931); the cover names no editor or arranger, and the only name on the page is Finlay Dun (died 1853), a maker of the song; the words are Lady Nairne's (died 1845), the other maker, though the page does not name her. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
